title: GBV Patterns
summary: An advocacy and research platform on femicide and gender-based violence, built with the Coalition Against Trafficking in Women, making the case for New York to become the first US state to name femicide in law.

contribution.roleNote: Built by the Ethical Tech CoLab at NYU with the Coalition Against Trafficking in Women (CATW); first shown at the Ethical Tech Summit, 20 November 2026.

narrative.problem: About three dozen countries define femicide in their criminal codes and no US state does. New York counts domestic violence homicides by borough and relationship, but a woman killed by a buyer, a pimp or a trafficker has no category to be counted in.
narrative.decision: Shows the Women Count USA databases only through their author's own published share links, rather than aggregating them, and keeps raw exports containing names, photos and narratives out of the repository.
narrative.tradeoff: Case-level patterns cannot be charted on the site until Dawn Wilcox and CATW agree in writing; until then visitors log counts by hand with a tally tool.
narrative.limitation: The number of femicides in the sex trade is unknown, not zero; county-level enforcement counts are not published, and the Progress page and BACKLOG.md list what is not yet built or researched.
narrative.caveat: Describes femicide, rape and trafficking, including real cases. Every figure links to its source; figures quoted from secondary summaries are flagged.
